findings.issue: character(:), allocatable was filed under C805, but that is a char-selector in the TYPE-SPEC (7.4.4.2), not a char-length in an entity-decl.
findings.resolution: Uses the entity-decl form deferred*(:), allocated with a length and checked by LEN and value.

findings.issue: integer :: x = n was filed as an R805 negative, but it is diagnosed because n is not a constant expression, governed by C1012.
findings.resolution: Withdrawn; R805's facet returns to pending with a C1012 note.

findings.issue: No permanent mutation runner; the unittest merely counted mutation definitions.

Four runtime mutants became non-conforming (type mismatch at a call, a declared length contradicting an ALLOCATE type-spec, a shape mismatch, an executable statement before declarations) and were counted as killed.
findings.resolution: Replaced with conforming mutants; the runner now rejects any compile-fail runtime mutant.

findings.issue: Remove-initializer mutants read undefined variables (9.2 p2, 19.6.3, 19.6.4), which is non-conforming evidence.
findings.resolution: Replaced with changed-initializer or later-assignment mutants that keep every variable defined.

findings.issue: The replacement for declared-type-across-list split the list and changed a VALUE, so it failed for the value, not the type.
findings.resolution: A generic interface with INTEGER and REAL specifics is called on BOTH list entities; the mutant real :: first = 11, second = 13 compiles and fails at run time for the type reason, and the reviewer confirmed the second entity is independently exercised.

lesson: Four rounds, every one about mutation or attribution rather than the oracles. A mutant must be CONFORMING (compile on the reference, read no undefined value) and must fail for the reason the facet names; removing an initializer is not a conforming mutation.
